welcomeDisclaimer.heading: Welcome to Yomu Academy
welcomeDisclaimer.message: This Season One story is AI-authored fiction: an invented composite, not biography, and not a claim that any depicted event happened in real life.
welcomeDisclaimer.sourceBoundary: Sanitized source patterns inspire learning themes and friendship energy only. Every scene, choice, joke, risk, location, and outcome is invented.
welcomeDisclaimer.likenessBoundary: A named cast member does not authorize a real likeness. Event art must obey the canonical likeness gate.

scope.groupingPolicy: One continuous season ordered by curriculum milestone; no academic-period grouping.
scope.finiteStoryRule: The Lantern Atlas plot resolves in episode 24. Later play reviews the completed story without adding canonical events.

relationshipThreads.arc: Mika and Peter welcome Felix through patient observation; Felix later returns that care by noticing quiet requests and making room before anyone has to perform confidence.
Different study speeds first feel like a hierarchy, then become complementary routes through the same challenge.
Belonging survives absence when the next useful place is left visible and genuinely open.

curriculum.milestone: greetings, classroom repair, and choosing a learning route

episodes.title: The Blank Atlas
episodes.storyBeat: Rie reveals a blank atlas for the Academy lantern exhibition. It will light only when learners fill it with Japanese gathered through shared challenges.
episodes.emotionalTurn: The pressure to sound ready eases when Rie treats a repair phrase as the first contribution rather than a mistake.

minigame.prompt: Choose the classroom phrase that keeps a greeting moving.
minigame.success: The first atlas lantern illuminates and the speaker receives a useful reply.

replayVariants.label: Soft voice
replayVariants.changes: Use quiet audio and a repetition repair.

replayVariants.label: Fast greeting
replayVariants.changes: Use natural-speed audio and a clarification repair.

eventArt.brief: Rie opens a large blank paper map as one lantern point appears above the library table.
eventArt.safety: Rie may use her approved design; pending classmates use neutral non-likeness staging.

sourceSafety.note: The atlas, exhibition, and welcome exchange are wholly invented.

curriculum.milestone: hiragana recognition and sustainable study routines

episodes.title: Map in the Margins
episodes.storyBeat: Henry finds that the atlas responds to handwritten kana, but his elaborate study system produces a route too crowded to read.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Henry expects admiration for complexity; honest editing preserves his idea and makes it useful to everyone.
episodes.comedyBeat: A five-step mnemonic for one kana needs its own index, appendix, and ceremonial pointer.

minigame.prompt: Trace the kana, then remove the detail that obscures its shape.
minigame.success: A readable route prints onto the atlas.

eventArt.brief: Clean kana cards surround one spectacularly over-annotated route card.
eventArt.safety: Use original props and neutral non-likeness classmates.

sourceSafety.note: The responsive map and study conflict are invented.

curriculum.milestone: directions, location words, and permission requests

episodes.title: Route Zero
episodes.storyBeat: Aakash leads a photo-word route, then discovers the atlas has removed every automatic label. He must ask the group for names and directions.
episodes.emotionalTurn: A test of independence becomes proof that asking for help creates more conversation, not less competence.
episodes.comedyBeat: A flawless request asks to photograph the bench while Aakash points grandly at a fountain.

minigame.prompt: Match each view to a location phrase and ask before collecting it.
minigame.success: Three negotiated landmarks join the atlas.

eventArt.brief: Aakash holds a label-free camera while friends point toward courtyard landmarks.
eventArt.safety: Use a fictional courtyard and a neutral non-likeness placeholder for Aakash.

sourceSafety.note: The route, camera failure, and requests are invented.

curriculum.milestone: pronunciation, listening discrimination, and clarification

episodes.title: The Welcome Frequency
episodes.storyBeat: Mika notices that one atlas lantern answers rhythm more reliably than volume. Her patient listening makes a route for softer voices.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Mika stops apologizing for taking time when the group recognizes careful listening as the skill that lets everyone enter.

minigame.prompt: Tap the mora rhythm, then clarify two close readings.
minigame.success: The lantern tunes itself to more voices.

eventArt.brief: Sound marks become lantern rings around a shared microphone as hands tap the beat.
eventArt.safety: Identify pending-likeness learners through nameplates and activity props.

sourceSafety.note: The responsive lantern and sound-room moment are invented.

curriculum.milestone: katakana, counters, and playful commands

episodes.title: Final Boss: One Small Card
episodes.storyBeat: Tom turns a katakana sort into an original tabletop quest. The impossible final card falls when the group reads its smallest clue.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Tom learns that spectacle works best when it leaves room for another person to find the answer.
episodes.comedyBeat: The victory ceremony for one sorted card lasts longer than the challenge.

minigame.prompt: Sort original item cards by sound and count the sets.
minigame.success: The party earns a route token together.

eventArt.brief: An original tabletop quest frames a tiny katakana card as a dramatic final challenge.
eventArt.safety: Invent all game symbols, cards, creatures, and interfaces.

sourceSafety.note: The game and victory are invented.

curriculum.milestone: time, routines, invitations, and respectful refusal

episodes.title: The Invitation Chain
episodes.storyBeat: Sam coordinates a small practice session, but each reply adds another option until lunch resembles a diplomatic summit.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Sam realizes a declined option is not rejected friendship; clear invitations make consent easier to hear.
episodes.comedyBeat: Two snack choices grow into a decision tree with an emergency karaoke branch.

minigame.prompt: Build an invitation and choose a respectful reply.
minigame.success: The group agrees on one achievable plan.

eventArt.brief: A cafe table is covered by a branching plan that resolves into one invitation card.
eventArt.safety: The cafe and plans are fictional and contain no private logistics.

sourceSafety.note: The invitation chain and cafe meeting are invented.

curriculum.milestone: past tense, opinions, and describing without naming

episodes.title: No Spoilers Beyond This Curtain
episodes.storyBeat: Francis hosts an original mystery-serial club, but one viewer is behind. The group must discuss clues without naming the reveal.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Francis stops treating taste as a verdict and uses questions that let quieter viewers build their own reading.
episodes.comedyBeat: Every safe synonym for the culprit sounds more suspicious than the forbidden answer.

minigame.prompt: Describe an original scene while avoiding the spoiler token.
minigame.success: The late viewer identifies the clue without losing the reveal.

eventArt.brief: Friends face a paused original lantern mystery behind a handmade spoiler curtain.
eventArt.safety: Use only original media, characters, costumes, and screen design.

sourceSafety.note: The serial, club, and spoiler problem are invented.

curriculum.milestone: food vocabulary, counters, preferences, and menu reading

episodes.title: The Menu Without Pictures
episodes.storyBeat: Shin receives a pictureless menu and turns components and readings into clues. The fanciest item proves to be the simplest dish.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Shin shares uncertainty between two readings, turning expertise from performance into investigation.
episodes.comedyBeat: A solemn debate over a rare delicacy ends at the tiny label: plain rice.

minigame.prompt: Combine a reading, counter, and preference to identify the order.
minigame.success: The correct dish card joins the feast route.

eventArt.brief: A fictional menu unfolds into ingredient, counter, and kanji clue cards.
eventArt.safety: Use invented dishes and branding-free menu design.

sourceSafety.note: The menu challenge and feast are invented.

curriculum.milestone: past and present description, comparison, and quoted thoughts

episodes.title: The Story in Two Tenses
episodes.storyBeat: Jodi finds two captions for one fictional photograph: what happened then and what the place means now. Both reveal the route.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Jodi makes room for several interpretations without forcing one memory to defeat another.

minigame.prompt: Pair a past action with a present-state caption.
minigame.success: The image gains depth and reveals a path.

eventArt.brief: One invented photograph has past-action and present-feeling caption ribbons.
eventArt.safety: The photograph and memory are fictional, with neutral figures.

sourceSafety.note: The gallery photograph and memories are invented.

curriculum.milestone: te-form sequences, instructions, and cause and effect

episodes.title: Instructions for a Cloud
episodes.storyBeat: Christian leads a weather-lantern build, but instruction cards drift out of order. The team must sequence them before the paper cloud opens.
episodes.emotionalTurn: An improvised repair shows Christian that instructions can guide people without silencing them.
episodes.comedyBeat: A valid sequence asks everyone to admire the empty table before attaching anything.

minigame.prompt: Order and speak the action cards.
minigame.success: The cloud lantern opens correctly.

eventArt.brief: Paper cloud pieces float above a workbench in visual sentence order.
eventArt.safety: Use original craft design and neutral non-likeness staging.

sourceSafety.note: The workshop and weather lantern are invented.

curriculum.milestone: plans, experience, travel language, and repair strategies

episodes.title: The Storm Route Variant
episodes.storyBeat: Alex enters an invented route simulation. A projected storm removes the signs, forcing a choice between pressing ahead and calling the team.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Alex names the fear of disappointing others, asks for support, and learns that changing a plan can be decisive.

minigame.prompt: Read changed signs, report the obstacle, and choose a safer fictional route.
minigame.success: Alex arrives through a route chosen with the team.

riskBeat.disclaimer: This wholly invented fictional variant does not describe or claim a real event.
riskBeat.agency: Alex pauses the simulation, asks the team for options, and chooses the revised route.

eventArt.brief: A tabletop route projection changes to rain symbols as Alex reaches a choice point.
eventArt.safety: Show a safe simulation with a pause control and a neutral non-likeness Alex.

sourceSafety.note: The route, projected weather, risk, and resolution are invented.

curriculum.milestone: offers, descriptions, work language, and requesting help

episodes.title: The Vanishing Course
episodes.storyBeat: Jenny leads an invented serving scene. The projected dish cards vanish, leaving her with a blank cue board and a choice to invite the ensemble in.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Jenny asks for help aloud; each classmate contributes one phrase, turning a failed solo into an ensemble success.

minigame.prompt: Offer an item, describe it, and request the missing cue.
minigame.success: The ensemble rebuilds the service sequence.

riskBeat.disclaimer: This wholly invented fictional variant does not describe or claim a real event.
riskBeat.agency: Jenny stops the solo format, requests support, and redesigns the scene as an ensemble.

eventArt.brief: Blank projected menu cards become phrase cards as classmates answer Jenny.
eventArt.safety: The countdown is theatrical, not physical danger; Jenny uses a neutral placeholder.

sourceSafety.note: The stage failure, pressure, and repair are invented.

curriculum.milestone: restaurant language, polite forms, and introductory conditionals

episodes.title: Dinner by If
episodes.storyBeat: Robert receives one rule: each cooking action unlocks after a correct if-sentence. A surprise fictional ingredient breaks the plan.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Robert gives up the perfect sequence and accepts a quieter learner's idea, making the shared dish better.
episodes.comedyBeat: A valid conditional sends everyone to garnish an empty plate with absolute seriousness.

minigame.prompt: Complete an if-sentence to choose the next action.
minigame.success: An improvised dish reaches the table.

eventArt.brief: Ingredients form a conditional sentence path ending at a shared dish.
eventArt.safety: Use a fictional recipe and no real venue or brand.

sourceSafety.note: The kitchen rules and outcome are invented.

curriculum.milestone: particles, evidence, reading, and explanation

episodes.title: Two Answers, One Context
episodes.storyBeat: Sophie finds two particles submitted for the atlas motto. She stages a context trial where each witness changes what listeners know.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Sophie lets go of one universal answer and delights in showing why both teams noticed useful evidence.
episodes.comedyBeat: Henry objects on dramatic grounds and learns that even objections need the right particle.

minigame.prompt: Choose a particle, then revise it when context changes.
minigame.success: The class writes two precise captions.

eventArt.brief: A mock court uses particle cards, context witnesses, and two caption boards.
eventArt.safety: The court is an invented lesson fantasy.

sourceSafety.note: The trial, dispute, and dialogue are invented.

curriculum.milestone: sound, listening, te-form recognition, and casual reactions

episodes.title: The Chorus With a Hole
episodes.storyBeat: Xingyu tests an original study song whose chorus contains a memorable grammar error. The class must preserve rhythm while repairing it.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Xingyu shares the flawed draft; laughter becomes affection when the wrong line helps everyone hear the distinction.
episodes.comedyBeat: The song treats a humble preparation phrase as an arena-anthem climax.

minigame.prompt: Find the mismatch and fit the correction into the beat.
minigame.success: The class performs an accurate original chorus.

eventArt.brief: A rehearsal room becomes an imagined concert while verb forms pulse on a lyric display.
eventArt.safety: Use original music, lyrics, and no artist or interface imitation.

sourceSafety.note: The song, error, and performance are invented.

curriculum.milestone: technology language, written questions, cause and effect, and repair

episodes.title: The Night the Map Went Dark
episodes.storyBeat: Angel connects the routes to a fictional tool. It follows an imprecise instruction literally and erases every visible path.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Angel expects blame, but the group separates a failed tool from its builder and finds the routes survive in teach-back.
episodes.comedyBeat: The help panel proudly says it reduced clutter by displaying nothing.

minigame.prompt: Compare intent with output and rewrite the instruction.
minigame.success: One route reappears, proving the work is recoverable.

eventArt.brief: The atlas darkens while one hand-drawn route remains beneath the projection.
eventArt.safety: Represent AI as a fallible, branding-free tool.

sourceSafety.note: The tool, shock, and recovery clue are invented.

curriculum.milestone: animal counters, relative clauses, observation, and polite requests

episodes.title: The Catwalk Clue
episodes.storyBeat: Felix joins the rebuild when a paper cat keeps appearing beside mislabeled cards. He sees that it follows the error pattern.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Felix fears his delight in the cat is distracting; Mika and Peter show that attention and joy uncovered the clue.
episodes.comedyBeat: The paper cat becomes supervisor and receives one counter, three titles, and no useful qualifications.

minigame.prompt: Describe each card and count clues sharing one error.
minigame.success: Felix identifies a recovery pattern.

eventArt.brief: Paper cats lead between word cards. Felix's canonical visual brief is a white classmate with glasses and longer curly dark-blond to light-brown hair, shown only after separate approval.
eventArt.safety: Felix has no approved visual evidence: use a nameplate, hands, cat props, or another non-portrait placeholder until approval. Never use a pre-existing unmatched face, and infer no further traits from appearance.

sourceSafety.note: Felix's puzzle, feelings, actions, and relationships are invented.

curriculum.milestone: kanji, personal expression, revision, and evidence

episodes.title: The Memory Card Museum
episodes.storyBeat: Stasi curates visual kanji memories for the rebuild. The funniest exhibit teaches a vivid false association.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Stasi chooses accuracy over applause, then finds joy when visitors submit clearer personal revisions.
episodes.comedyBeat: The correction is less majestic but so oddly specific that nobody forgets it.

minigame.prompt: Test a memory image and repair one misleading detail.
minigame.success: A verified card restores one district.

eventArt.brief: Original mnemonic pictures surround one decisive red-pencil correction.
eventArt.safety: Use Yomu's own visual language and no recognizable artist style.

sourceSafety.note: The museum, exhibits, and response are invented.

curriculum.milestone: subtitles, inference, ambiguity, and partial comprehension

episodes.title: Seventy Percent Is a Door
episodes.storyBeat: Ruparna plays an original mystery clip above the class's comfort level. When subtitles fail, they infer from tone and known words.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Apparent unreadiness becomes proof that incomplete understanding can still support precise inference and joy.
episodes.comedyBeat: A dramatic confession becomes a sandwich order because one food word wins the sentence.

minigame.prompt: Mark anchors, compare visual evidence, and choose the supported meaning.
minigame.success: The route opens without pretending every word was understood.

eventArt.brief: Known words light around an original animated mystery frame with useful gaps.
eventArt.safety: Use wholly original media and no third-party interface.

sourceSafety.note: The clip, subtitle failure, and inferences are invented.

curriculum.milestone: lived-memory language, work language, comparison, and sequence

episodes.title: A Map Made From Memory
episodes.storyBeat: Rose asks each learner to describe a recovered route as change in a garden. Their accounts overlap into a richer map.
episodes.emotionalTurn: The class stops mourning a perfect copy and accepts that shared memory can preserve different perspectives.

minigame.prompt: Sequence change cards and compare two route accounts.
minigame.success: The atlas regrows as a layered garden map.

eventArt.brief: Garden paths overlay translucent route descriptions from several learners.
eventArt.safety: Use a fictional garden and invented memories.

sourceSafety.note: The garden, accounts, and reconstruction are invented.

curriculum.milestone: review, questions, observation, and teach-back

episodes.title: Questions in the Dark
episodes.storyBeat: Peter proposes rebuilding a district without projection. Each learner may ask one strong question before teaching an answer back.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Peter's observation becomes leadership, while Felix notices who has not spoken and passes over the final question.

minigame.prompt: Choose the question that removes most uncertainty.
minigame.success: The class reconstructs the district from dialogue.

eventArt.brief: Question cards glow around a paper atlas as the final card is passed onward.
eventArt.safety: Use hands, name cards, and non-identifiable silhouettes for pending likenesses.

sourceSafety.note: The dark-room constraint and dialogue are invented.

curriculum.milestone: casual speech, register shifts, game dialogue, and belonging

episodes.title: The Blank Space on the Board
episodes.storyBeat: Shaun arrives after the rebuild is nearly complete and sees no role. He notices the game route stays formal during a pastry collapse.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Feeling unnecessary gives way to belonging when Shaun's ear for casual dialogue makes the rebuilt world feel alive.
episodes.comedyBeat: A hero fleeing a pastry avalanche delivers a formal greeting to every bun.

minigame.prompt: Rewrite an over-formal line for the fictional scene.
minigame.success: The route gains natural social texture.

replayVariants.label: Friendly scene
replayVariants.changes: Shift lines to warm casual speech.

eventArt.brief: A project board leaves one blank dialogue panel beside an original pastry game.
eventArt.safety: Do not depict a reason for absence; use a neutral Shaun placeholder.

sourceSafety.note: The arrival, game world, feelings, and contribution are invented.

curriculum.milestone: plans, before-and-after clauses, gratitude, and unfinished intentions

episodes.title: The Farewell Rehearsal
episodes.storyBeat: Nanako says her atlas guide role ends after the exhibition. The group scripts a farewell meal so fragile that one late lantern breaks it.
episodes.emotionalTurn: They abandon perfection, share imperfect dishes, and voice postponed gratitude. Sadness remains beside warmth.
episodes.comedyBeat: Henry's contingency board contains more arrows than food and one unexplained karaoke loop.

minigame.prompt: Complete an intention and choose a caring response.
minigame.success: The table becomes the final route into the exhibition.

replayVariants.label: Next plan
replayVariants.changes: Focus on future intention without logistics.

eventArt.brief: An imperfect table glows beneath tangled plans and handwritten gratitude cards.
eventArt.safety: The departure, meal, schedule, and setting are fictional; include no travel detail.

sourceSafety.note: Nanako's role change, farewell, and emotions are invented.

curriculum.milestone: integrated review, inference, conditionals, register, and narration

episodes.title: When the Lanterns Return
episodes.storyBeat: The rebuilt atlas will not light. Mira realizes the final route is an action: the class must narrate its shared routes in Japanese.
episodes.emotionalTurn: Mira fears joining late means she cannot matter; her contextual insight becomes the key, and every voice completes the story.
episodes.comedyBeat: Everyone poses beside the dark atlas as if determination might become visible.

minigame.prompt: Infer the action and connect one remembered clue to the next speaker.
minigame.success: All routes illuminate; the finite story resolves and calendar review unlocks.

eventArt.brief: The paper atlas fills a hall with distinct lantern routes as the ensemble forms a circle.
eventArt.safety: Use approved likenesses only; all others require neutral figures or activity-led framing.

sourceSafety.note: The exhibition, final puzzle, action, and resolution are invented.

endlessCalendar.purpose: Generate years of spaced, varied review from the resolved story without inventing later canonical plot.
endlessCalendar.dayTemplateRule: The seven templates repeat across all four cycle accents; dayOfCycle is offset by seven for each accent.

castRotation.algorithm: Choose the least-recently-featured eligible member, then a relationship-thread partner; break ties with the deterministic seed.
castRotation.felixRule: Felix rotates through listening, animal-counter, observation, and relationship-thread reviews; cat comedy is occasional rather than his sole topic.

longRangeRemix.effect: Recombine one Foundation, one N5, and one N4 hook into an original review festival with no new canonical outcome.
longRangeRemix.yearlyContinuity: Cycle counts may grow without limit; progress records mastery and friendship review, never a new plot date or biographical claim.

continuityRules: The atlas remains complete after the finale.
Calendar scenes are practice remixes, not canonical sequels.
No calendar result changes an introduction, unlock, relationship outcome, or Season One ending.
All media, songs, games, costumes, locations, and event art remain original and likeness-gated.
